Position: Marketing Manager

Location: West Jordan, UT

We're hiring a Marketing Manager to lead the day-to-day marketing effort at Rust. You'll work with leadership to set priorities, then turn those priorities into campaigns, content, events, and tools that help our sales teams and manufacturer partners be more effective.

This is a hands-on role with a lot of variety: trade shows, manufacturer marketing, digital campaigns, content, sales materials, and our website. You won't be doing it alone. We already have marketing support, an internal development team, established manufacturer relationships, and leadership that is invested in making marketing a stronger part of the business.

Role & Responsibilities

Marketing strategy and planning

Work with leadership to set marketing priorities, including the markets we focus on, manufacturer lines we promote, how we position ourselves, and where we spend our time and budget. Then turn those priorities into action.

Trade shows and events

Manage industry shows, customer training events, and vendor events from start to finish, including booth logistics, pre-show outreach, lead capture, staffing, follow-up, and measuring results.

Manufacturer and vendor marketing

Work with our manufacturer partners on co-op marketing funds, joint campaigns, product launches, line cards, and literature. Make sure we're representing their brands well and taking advantage of the resources they provide.

Demand generation

Manage paid media, SEO, email campaigns, content, landing pages, and list building. Track performance and understand what these efforts are producing.

Sales enablement

Create and manage line cards, spec sheets, case studies, presentations, and other materials our sales teams use in the field. The goal is simple: give our salespeople tools that are useful and that they actually want to use.

Swag, literature, and fulfillment

Manage Rust and vendor swag, printed literature, and line cards. Forecast what our sales teams and branches will need, coordinate orders, work with vendors, and keep materials organized and available.

Brand and content

Maintain a consistent voice and look across everything we put out, including customer stories, LinkedIn, newsletters, website content, and PR where it makes sense.

Measuring results

Track things like pipeline contribution, cost per lead, cost per quote, campaign performance, and where our marketing dollars are going.

What makes this role different

Manufacturer partnerships are a big part of the job

We're a partner-led business, so working with our manufacturer partners is an important part of marketing here. That includes brand standards, co-op dollars, product launches, joint campaigns, and other marketing programs.

Experience on the manufacturer or distributor side is a plus, but it's not required.

Qualifications & Profile

We're flexible on how you got here. Any of these could be a good fit:

- Marketing management at an industrial distributor, manufacturer's representative, manufacturer, or another technical industry
- A strong marketing specialist or manager at a larger industrial company who's ready for more responsibility
- Agency experience serving industrial clients, if you're ready to come in-house and work more directly with the business and its results

Deep trade show and event experience is a real plus. So is experience working with manufacturer partners and joint marketing programs.

A relevant degree, equivalent experience, or a track record that speaks for itself can all work here. We care more about what you've built and how you work than exactly where you learned it.

You like people.

This job puts you in front of customers, manufacturer partners, and our own team constantly. Trade show floors, booth duty, dinners, meetings, and plenty of conversations. It isn't a desk job with a campaign calendar.

You finish things.

There are a lot of moving pieces in marketing. You need to be organized, keep things moving, close loops, and follow through.

You take responsibility.

You'll have support and a solid foundation to work from, but you'll be responsible for keeping your areas moving and making sure things get done.

You bring ideas and can execute them.

We want someone who will look at what we're doing and find ways to make it better. At the same time, you'll need to be comfortable taking an established program and executing it well without feeling like everything needs to be redesigned first.

You're comfortable with technical people.

You don't need an engineering degree. You do need to be curious about what a flow meter or control panel actually does and comfortable sitting down with an engineer and asking questions.

You're honest about the numbers.

If a campaign didn't work, tell us. We'd rather learn from it than find a way to make the numbers look better.

- Exemplify what "great" looks like in your work?
- Thrive on solving problems and tackling challenges?

- Serve as the executive SEO advisor and provide executive-level strategy during client planning and quarterly business reviews

- Mentor Strategists and Specialists while elevating the overall quality of SEO deliverables

- Partner with leadership on service development and innovation

About this role

AI is fundamentally changing how product strategy and market strategy work together. The boundary between building the right product and bringing it to market the right way is disappearing — and the companies that recognize this will build product marketing functions that operate as strategic growth engines, not service organizations.

ActiveCampaign’s Active Intelligence platform — autonomous AI agents serving 180,000+ growing businesses — is redefining how marketing works. We need a Director of Product Marketing who shapes how the market understands it through bold storytelling, drives adoption that compounds, and transforms the PMM discipline in the process.

This role reports to the SVP of Product. Product and Product Marketing operate as a single strategic arm — you’ll have the same context as the people building the product and the same accountability for what happens when it meets the market. This is a player-coach role: you lead a team, but you also personally create — strategies, narratives, content, programs. AI makes that possible at a level it never was before, and we expect our leaders to use it.

Why This Role Matters:

The way companies build, market, and grow products is being reshaped by AI. Product Marketing must evolve from a support function into a strategic operating system for customer understanding, market differentiation, and intelligent go-to-market execution. At ActiveCampaign, we’re building that now. This role is at the center of it.

On a typical day, you might:

- Market Narrative & Positioning:

- Define and evolve positioning that clearly articulates why Active Intelligence represents a fundamentally new way for businesses to run their marketing — and why that matters now.
- Translate complex AI capabilities into clear, compelling customer value that resonates across segments.
- Bring conviction to the narrative — if the story isn’t bold enough, make it bolder. We want a PMM leader whose point of view strengthens every room they’re in.
- Adoption & Customer Outcomes:

- Lead go-to-market strategies measured by adoption and continued usage, not launch ceremony. Your success is customers who build their business on Active Intelligence.
- Own the market-side of the customer lifecycle — the narrative that moves someone from “I tried it” to “I can’t turn this off.” Partner with Product to build both sides of that engine.
- Run experimentation-driven programs: every initiative has a hypothesis, a signal, and a learning cycle. We move in weekly learning cycles, not quarterly planning windows.
- AI-First Execution:

- Automate traditional launch mechanics — release notes, enablement decks, internal comms. Your team operates above the automation line.
- Leverage AI to transform how the PMM craft works, not just what it produces. Speed, experimentation, and operational scale improve by default.
- Sales, Partner & Revenue Enablement:

- Arm Sales, CS, and our partner ecosystem with positioning, proof points, and talk tracks that improve conversations and conversion.
- Establish feedback loops between GTM teams and Product — friction points and market opportunities flow back into product decisions.
- Evangelism & Market Authority:

- Build the market presence that makes ActiveCampaign the reference point for autonomous marketing — thought leadership, proof points, and narrative formats that establish our position.
- Team Leadership:

- Lead a PMM team of outcome owners who own strategic priorities the way PMs own product areas — with backlogs, experiments, and shipped impact.
- Set the standard by doing the work yourself, not just directing it. The best PMM leaders we’ve seen create alongside their teams — AI makes that leverage real.
- Build a culture of accountability, ownership, and urgency. Create clarity in ambiguity and drive alignment through influence and results.
- Invest in your people’s growth as seriously as the work itself — create conditions where they do the best work of their careers in service to their individual and collective success.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Required:

- 8+ years of hands-on experience in Product Marketing, Growth, or Product Strategy in B2B SaaS or AI-driven technology companies.
- 3+ years of proven leadership experience leading PMM teams — experience building or transforming a function, not just running one.
- A product-strategy mindset: you think about market impact the way great PMs think about product-market fit.
- A proven track record driving adoption and retention outcomes, not just launch metrics.
- Proven ability to influence across Product, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success.

Highly Valued:

- Prior experience with AI-native products, marketing automation, or platform products serving SMB/mid-market
- Experience building experimentation-driven marketing functions.
- Deep customer empathy paired with analytical rigor.
- A mindset that thinks beyond launches — you understand how product marketing drives company growth.
- A desire to erase the artificial boundary between product and marketing.
- An AI-native approach in how you think, work, and lead — not just AI-curious.
- A bias for action and execution: you’d rather build the positioning doc yourself than wait for someone to draft it. Leading a team doesn’t mean you stop creating.
- The ability to build trust through clarity, accountability, and results. You care about outcomes, not organizational theater.
- A passion for transformation rather than maintenance.

What Success Looks Like:

Within 3–6 months, you will have:

- Established Product Marketing as a strategic growth function trusted by Product, GTM, and leadership.
- Driven measurable improvement in product adoption, continued usage, and customer expansion.
- Sharpened market and product positioning to the point where customers deeply understand the step-change innovation we’re delivering and how it transforms their business.
- Built a modern PMM operating model — a team of leaders fully leveraging AI in everything they do, oriented around measurable business outcomes.

Director, Product Marketing

We’re looking for a Director of Product Marketing to own how Help Scout tells its story in a crowded, fast-growing market – shaping the positioning, narrative, and go-to-market strategy that define how customers, prospects, and the industry understand our platform.

It’s an exciting time to be here. With a new vision and an AI-driven vision, we’ll be shipping more products faster to ensure we can quickly meet the changing needs of the market. You’ll set the strategy for how we position that pace of innovation, build the frameworks that help the whole company talk about it credibly, and make sure our AI-driven product investments land as real value in the market not just feature noise. - Own product marketing strategy. Set and execute the quarterly and long-term strategy for how Help Scout positions its product and platform, informed by market trends, competitive analytics, and where the company is headed.

- Build and scale the product marketing function. Manage and partner with our Lead Product Marketing Manager, setting priorities, coaching on craft, and creating room for them to grow into owning larger initiatives. You’ll help build the team’s roadmap for headcount and capability over the next 12-18 months.

- Enable the whole company. Ensure sales, support, and teammates across Help Scout have what they need to understand and clearly articulate the value of what we ship. - Shape competitive intelligence at a strategic level. - Own major product launches and seasonal release events end-to-end. Set the strategy and narrative arc for product release events and other major launches, coordinating across Sales, Product, Support, and Marketing to land them with impact.

- Represent Help Scout’s product story externally. Use guest posts, podcasts, social, and other channels to build the company’s external visibility and reputation as a category leader, both for the platform and for how we’re building it.

About you

- You have significant experience in product marketing for a B2B SaaS product or AI platform, with a track record of owning strategy, not just executing campaigns.

- You’re an expert in every core discipline of product marketing: positioning, messaging, buyer personas/ICP, sales enablement, and launches, and you can identify which high-value activities matter most for the business right now.

- You’ve managed people before, and know how to coach someone on craft, give them room to own real work, and help them grow into more senior responsibility.

- You have a point of view on positioning AI-powered products credibly, and ideally have direct experience marketing AI features or products.

- You use AI tools daily to improve your own output and your team’s, and you can point to specific examples where AI changed the speed, quality, or scale of what you or your team delivered.

Apply

About Ethos

Ethos (Nasdaq: $LIFE) is a leading life insurance technology company on a mission to protect families by democratizing access to life insurance and empowering agents at scale. With its robust three-sided technology platform, Ethos is transforming the life insurance experience for consumers, agents, and carriers alike. Ethos offers instant, accessible products and a seamless online process that requires no medical exams and just a few health questions; it eliminates traditional barriers, making it easier than ever for everyone to protect their families. Ethos is redefining how life insurance is bought, sold, and underwritten.

About the role

We are seeking a data-obsessed, US-based Senior Growth Marketing Manager to own the lifecycle across three distinct customer journeys: converting prospects into customers, expanding existing customers through cross-sell and upsell, and scaling a recently launched product line. The through-line is conversion, retention, and maximizing long-term customer value (LTV).

These three journeys work differently, and that's the interesting part of the job. Prospect-to-customer conversion is a blend of self-serve digital and human follow-up — live agents and voice AI — so your job is to design what gets said, to whom, and when, so that confidence keeps building in the gaps between conversations. Cross-sell, upsell, and the new product line are entirely self-serve. There is no human in the loop, which means the messaging, the timing, and the on-page experience have to carry the entire decision on their own.

Life insurance is a high-consideration purchase, so lack of trust and product understanding are the biggest drivers of drop-off. Across all three journeys, you own the connective tissue that moves someone from "a company I found on the internet" to "a company I trust to safeguard my future." You will operate on shared OKRs with the product managers who own each of these three areas, and — for the conversion journey — in close working partnership with Sales leadership, agents, and our voice AI team. You need to know what's actually landing on live calls, not just what performs in an inbox.

Duties and Responsibilities:

- Own the Lifecycle Strategy and Messaging. Design the narrative, cadence, and channel mix that carries someone from first touch to funded policy, from first policy to second, and from early interest in a new product line to scaled adoption. You set the strategy and you build it.
- Convert Prospects into Customers. Own the post-lead journey where self-serve and human touch meet. Build the digital nurture that moves people forward on their own, and build the follow-up content, sequences, and talking points that make every agent and voice AI conversation land — the right articles, proof points, or next steps that can go out within minutes of a call ending, and a system that gets smarter over time rather than sending the same packet to everyone.
- Drive Cross-Sell and Upsell. Existing customers are our highest-intent audience and this motion is fully self-serve. Own identifying the right next product for the right customer at the right moment — additional coverage, product upgrades, a second policy for a spouse — and build the triggered messaging, on-page experiences, and offer structures that get them there without a human touch.
- Scale a Recently Launched Product Line. We have a new product line in market and the mandate is growth. Own its self-serve lifecycle end to end: activation, onboarding, and the messaging that turns early traction into a repeatable, scaling funnel. This is 0→1 becoming 1→10, with the ambiguity and speed that implies.
- Own Retention and LTV. Getting someone to buy is the beginning, not the end. Own the post-purchase journey that keeps policies in force and customers engaged, and be accountable for LTV as a number you move, not a metric you report.
- Build Trust Signals Across the Funnel. Partner with Marketing and Product on the things that actually move a high-consideration financial decision: credibility and social proof, carrier proof points, reviews, and transparency about what someone is actually buying.
- Own the Data Behind Conversion and Drop-Off. Be the expert on cohorts and funnel curves across all three areas. Pull your own data to find exactly where trust and momentum break down, not just where a campaign underperforms — then turn that into a concrete hypothesis and test it.
- Run Experiments End to End. Test messaging, cadence, offers, and channel mix; report on statistical significance; roll out what wins.
- Cross-Functional Ownership. Operate on shared OKRs with the product managers across all three areas, and in a real working relationship with Sales leadership on the conversion journey. Decisions get made, ownership is felt, and campaigns don't stall because nobody knows who's driving.
- Scope. Your time splits across all three journeys with the weighting shifting as each area matures.

Qualifications and Skills:

- 6+ Years of Experience. Senior-level track record in Lifecycle, Growth Marketing, or CRM at a B2C Tech, FinTech, Insurtech, or Marketplace company. Higher-consideration / higher-AOV product experience strongly preferred.
- Copywriting and Messaging Strategy. You can write subject lines that get opened and body copy that drives action — and you know how to build trust and clarity into a high-consideration financial decision, not just optimize for clicks.
- Self-Serve Conversion Instincts. You've moved customers through a purchase decision with no human in the loop and you know what that demands: the messaging, the timing, and the on-page experience all have to do the persuading.
- Comfortable Partnering with a Sales Org. For the conversion journey, you want to know what's actually said on a live call, and you can translate that into content and tools that make agents and voice AI more effective — not assets built in isolation from what's happening in the field.
- Multi-Channel Mindset. You think natively across email, SMS, voice / conversational AI, in-product, on-page, and human-delivered follow-up. You do not believe email is the center of the universe.
- Analytical Mindset. Fluent in cohort retention, statistical significance, and LTV. Ability to self service data pulls/queries to find where trust and momentum break down in the funnel.

By the 1970s, the travel industry had quietly figured out something that most businesses hadn't: growth at scale required three different go-to-market motions happening at once. Individual travelers booked directly — they walked in, called up, and bought. Corporate travel programs needed a sales rep to negotiate rates and sign contracts. And then there were travel agents: independent businesses with deep client relationships who effectively decided what their clients bought. The airlines and hotel chains that grew fastest were the ones that recognized all of these distribution motions and invested in each of them in the right ways.

Mercury runs the same three motions. Most of our growth is self-serve and product-led: Founders discover us, sign up, and stay. Our fast-growing sales team closes meaningful deals with larger businesses. And our partners — incorporators, accountants, investors, and platforms that already have the trust of the businesses we want to reach — refer customers to us the same way a great travel agent would: because they believe in our product and its value to their clients. We are looking for a go-to-market leader who can make all three of these motions work harder together with a data-driven strategy and consistent positioning across the customer journey.

The Role

We're hiring a Marketing Manager to help keep LumiMeds' marketing organized, aligned, and moving forward across channels.

You'll work closely with leadership and channel specialists to turn company priorities into clear marketing plans and make sure those plans are executed well. You'll coordinate the day-to-day marketing function, manage timelines and workflows, review work before it goes live, and help ensure our messaging stays consistent across paid, organic, email, social, content, creative, and other channels.

The role is execution-focused, but you'll also contribute to marketing planning and help leadership identify opportunities, gaps, and priorities.

Because LumiMeds operates in a regulated category, you'll help ensure established marketing and compliance requirements are incorporated throughout the planning and review process.

What You'll Do

- Work with leadership to translate company priorities into marketing plans and campaigns.
- Manage the day-to-day marketing function across paid acquisition, organic content, SEO, email, social, partnerships, creative, and other initiatives.

- Turn marketing plans into execution, assigning owners, tracking progress, resolving blockers, and keeping initiatives moving.
- Review marketing work before launch for overall quality, messaging, audience fit, brand consistency, and adherence to established compliance guidelines.
- Apply strong marketing judgment across channels, asking the right questions and identifying weak strategy, unclear messaging, funnel gaps, or execution issues before they become bigger problems.
- Keep marketing unified across channels, ensuring teams aren't operating in silos or sending conflicting messages.
- Create and improve marketing processes for planning, briefs, reviews, approvals, launches, reporting, and cross-functional collaboration.
- Manage the marketing calendar and project pipeline, keeping high-priority campaigns and initiatives on track.
- Monitor performance across channels and work with specialists to understand what's working, what isn't, and what should change.
- Help connect the customer journey across channels, from first touch through conversion and ongoing communication.
- Coordinate with product, clinical, legal/compliance, design, customer support, and leadership on cross-functional initiatives.
- Manage agencies, freelancers, vendors, and external partners as needed.
- Provide leadership with clear visibility into marketing priorities, progress, results, risks, and upcoming initiatives.
- Identify gaps and opportunities across the marketing function and help determine what needs attention next.

What You Bring

- 3–6 years of hands-on marketing experience, ideally in a fast-moving consumer, DTC, subscription, healthcare, wellness, or technology business.
- Experience working across more than one marketing discipline or channel.
- A strong working knowledge of paid acquisition, lifecycle/email, content, SEO, social, creative, landing pages, conversion, and customer journeys.
- Strong marketing judgment. You understand audiences, positioning, offers, messaging, funnels, and channel strategy well enough to evaluate work and give useful feedback.
- Ability to look at marketing from both the customer perspective and the business perspective.
- Comfort reviewing marketing performance and understanding core metrics across different channels.
- Experience coordinating multiple campaigns, projects, or workstreams at the same time.
- Experience managing projects, agencies, contractors, or small teams.
- Strong project management and organizational skills. You can take a messy set of priorities and turn it into a clear plan.
- Strong quality-control instincts and the ability to identify work that is unclear, inconsistent, off-brand, poorly targeted, or potentially noncompliant.
- Ability to learn and apply detailed compliance and brand guidelines in a regulated marketing environment.
- Strong communication skills and confidence giving constructive feedback to specialists who may have deeper expertise in their individual channels.
- High ownership, curiosity, follow-through, and attention to detail.
- Comfortable operating in an early-stage environment where priorities can change quickly.

Bonus

- Telehealth, healthcare, pharmaceutical, wellness, or other regulated-industry experience.
- Experience with subscription or e-commerce businesses.
- Experience building marketing workflows or processes from scratch.
- Experience reviewing regulated advertising or working alongside legal/compliance teams.
- Experience managing external agencies or marketing vendors.
- Familiarity with tools such as Asana, Google Analytics, Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, CRM/email platforms, SEO tools, or similar marketing systems.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means:

- Marketing projects have clear owners, deadlines, and priorities.
- Specialists understand how their work connects to broader company goals.
- Campaigns move from idea to launch efficiently and with fewer last-minute issues.
- Paid, organic, email, social, content, and other channels feel like one cohesive marketing organization.
- Marketing work is reviewed thoughtfully before launch, with brand and compliance considerations built into the process.
- Weak messaging, funnel gaps, and execution issues are caught early.
- Leadership has clear visibility into what marketing is doing, why, and how initiatives are performing.
- Specialists have the structure, context, and support they need to do strong work.
- Marketing processes become more organized, efficient, and scalable as LumiMeds grows.

If this role sounds like a fit, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your application in English and ensure your resume reflects relevant experience for the role.

This position is open to candidates based in approved locations, depending on the role and business needs. Qualified applicants will be contacted for next steps.

- Demonstrated ability to lead major product launches end-to-end, from strategy through cross-functional execution and post-launch measurement.

- A strategic, big-picture orientation — genuinely energized by shaping direction and setting the strategy, rather than only executing against someone else's.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting to senior and executive stakeholders.

- Depth in market research, data-as-a-service, or consumer/data intelligence go-to-market is a strong plus — several of our most important narratives sit squarely in that territory.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any.
You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.
Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere.
We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like
Own a set of DTC accounts
as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
Own the client relationship.
There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
Audit before you touch anything.
Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
Run brand and non brand as different businesses.
Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
Know what PMax is actually doing.
The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
Keep Google's automation on a leash.
Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
Own the feed.
Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
Own the tracking.
GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.
Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
Build the things the account needs.
Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
You are a fit if
You have done this with real money.
Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
You are fluent in the whole stack
, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
You are AI native, and you build.
This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.
You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
You are skeptical of your own numbers.
You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.
Where you live is up to you.
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
You are not a fit if
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
You want to be told what to do this week.
You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
Benefits
Why this role is exciting
This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

ClearGov is building the modern financial operating layer for the public sector.

We help US local governments and school districts plan, budget, report, and communicate their finances with clarity and confidence. From long-term planning to financial reporting, compliance, and transparency, our platform connects the work finance teams are already doing and makes it easier to deliver for their communities.

Today, more than 2,000 public sector organizations use ClearGov, and we continue to expand our platform and reach as we grow. Our Core Values

- Be Clear & Credible
  - We are authentic in our interactions, communicating with clarity, speaking with honesty, and following through with consistency. We turn transparency into our greatest competitive advantage.
- Be Human
  - We are human partners to our colleagues and customers and lead with consideration and kindness - making space for others to do the same. We turn empathy into a shared strength.
- Be Better Together
  - We are committed to building an inclusive community where everyone thrives. We share successes, support each other through challenges, and show up for our teammates the way we show up for our customers. We turn togetherness into our greatest advantage and collaboration into our greatest multiplier.
- Be Honourable/Honorable
  - We are responsible to our colleagues and customers. We bring our full selves to every conversation, every project, every decision, and every relationship. We act with intention, deliver on our commitments, and lead with integrity - even when no one is watching. We turn honour into the foundation that powers everything we do.
- Be Connected
  - We are culture builders where people are seen, welcomed, and celebrated. We show up in every interaction - the laughs, the wins, the hard days. We turn connection into opportunities for people to feel they belong.

What Makes You a Great Fit

- You take ownership and follow through
- You communicate clearly and effectively
- You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out
- You learn quickly and adapt as things change
- You care about the team, not just your own work
- You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do

About the Opportunity

We're looking for a Manager, Growth & Customer Marketing to lead a team of two and own ClearGov's full-funnel growth motion — from a prospect's first touch through expansion revenue with existing customers. You'll manage and develop a team of two: one teammate focused on inbound (SEO/AEO) and net-new ABM/ABX campaigns, the other on customer marketing for cross-sell and upsell. You inherit both with real runway to grow in scope and title as the team's results build.

This is a player-coach role. You'll set the strategy, coach your team, and own the numbers — while staying hands-on with the highest-leverage campaigns and content yourself.

We need someone who is AI-forward by default: you use AI tools to move faster on content, targeting, SEO/AEO research, and reporting as a matter of course, and you build that habit into how your team works, not just how you work. You're proactive — you spot the SEO gap, the underperforming segment, or the expansion signal in the data before anyone points it out, and you act on it.

Key Responsibilities: Team Leadership

- Hire (as needed), coach, and manage a team of 2 marketers — one owning acquisition (inbound/SEO/AEO, ABM/ABX), one owning customer marketing (cross-sell/upsell) — with regular 1:1s, clear goals, and a development plan that gives each a real path to grow.
- Set quarterly growth marketing strategy and OKRs spanning net-new pipeline and expansion revenue; report results to marketing leadership.
- Operate as a player-coach: personally lead ClearGov's highest-priority campaigns and strategic accounts while delegating day-to-day execution to your team.
- Proactively surface and act on growth opportunities across the funnel — SEO/AEO gaps, underperforming ABM segments, expansion or churn-risk signals in customer health data — rather than waiting for them to be flagged.

Acquisition & Demand Generation

- Own ClearGov's inbound strategy — SEO and AEO (optimizing for AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, in addition to traditional search) — to grow organic visibility and traffic.
- Build and run ABM/ABX programs for net-new prospects, coordinating email, webinars, social, and content into unified account-based campaigns.
- Partner with Sales to align target account lists, campaign timing, and lead hand-off criteria for ABM-sourced pipeline.

Customer Marketing

- Own the full post-sale marketing motion — customer touchpoints (newsletter, product launch announcements, webinars), in-app announcements, and expansion/cross-sell campaigns from audience segmentation through performance measurement.
- Build and manage ClearGov's customer reference and advocacy program; lead the creation of case studies, video testimonials, and social proof.
- Track and report on expansion campaign performance — influenced pipeline, conversion rates, and contribution to upsell/cross-sell revenue.

AI & Ways of Working

- Use AI tools daily to speed up content production, campaign personalization, SEO/AEO research, and reporting — and build this into how your team operates, not just how you work individually.
- Bring a testing mindset: run experiments across channels and let data decide what gets more investment.

Critical Skills/Experience:

- 5–7+ years in B2B SaaS marketing, including 1–2+ years directly managing people — this is a people-management role from day one, not a step toward one.
- Full-funnel growth marketing experience with a track record you can show numbers for — growing net-new pipeline (SEO/AEO, ABM/ABX, demand gen) and growing expansion revenue (NRR, cross-sell/upsell).
- Hands-on SEO experience and working knowledge of AEO/answer-engine optimization — how content gets discovered by both traditional search and AI answer engines.
- Experience building and running ABM/ABX programs across email, webinars, and social; familiarity with intent/ABM platforms (6sense, Demandbase, or similar) a plus.
- Demonstrated, regular use of AI tools in a marketing workflow — content generation, personalization, research, or reporting — not just occasional experimentation.
- Hands-on proficiency with a marketing automation platform (Marketo, HubSpot, or similar) and comfort using CRM data (Salesforce preferred) to segment audiences and measure performance.
- Strong content and storytelling skills across formats — case studies, campaign copy, webinar scripts, video.
- Experience in a SaaS environment; GovTech or public sector experience is a plus, but not required.

Compensation:

execution-first growth
role.

Positioning, Feature Messaging & Launch Execution

Enrichment, AI Scoring & Routing

•    Own lead and account routing rules, handoff SLAs, and alerts to Sales and Customer Growth, and monitor speed-to-lead and conversion by route.
Demand Generation Experiments
•    Run a structured demand-gen experimentation program: define the hypothesis, audience, channel, offer, success metric, and decision rule before launch, then scale or move to the next experiment based on results.
•    Build and execute campaigns, nurture tracks, and outbound sequences against enriched, scored segments, partnering with the Digital Marketing Manager on creative and channel execution.
•    Use customer, competitive, and market insight to surface new segments and opportunities worth testing, and maintain a prioritized backlog and a visible results log so learnings compound.
Lifecycle & In-App Engagement
•    Own lifecycle programs across the customer journey: onboarding, activation, feature adoption, cross-sell and expansion, renewal, and win-back.
•    Build behavior-triggered journeys that combine CRM email and telemetry in-app guides, driven by product usage signals rather than calendar cadence alone.

Funnel Reporting & Measurement
•    Support maintenance of funnel stage definitions and conversion logic from first touch through closed-won, activation, and expansion.

•    Technical comfort beyond the UI: SQL, APIs and webhooks, or light scripting (JavaScript or Python) to connect systems and automate workflows.
•    Comfort building AI-powered workflows for research, enrichment, scoring, and content variation. You know how to make AI your copilot, not your copywriter.

We're at an exciting inflection point, taking decades of experience in childcare and child nutrition and using it to build a broader ecosystem of products for the organizations and people who help care for our communities.

Twin Health

At Twin Health, we empower people to improve and prevent chronic metabolic diseases, like type 2 diabetes and obesity, with a new standard of care. Twin Health is the only company applying AI Digital Twin technology exclusively toward metabolic health.

We start by building a dynamic model of each person’s metabolism — drawing on thousands of data points from CGMs, smartwatches, and meal logs — that maps their personal path to better health. Working here

Our team at Twin Health is passionate, talented, and united by a shared purpose: to improve the metabolic health and happiness of our members. We believe in empowering every Twin to make a meaningful impact for our members, our clients, and each other, while enjoying a supportive, collaborative work environment.

Twin has been recognized not only for our innovation but also for our culture, including: Innovator of the Year by the Employer Health Innovation Roundtable (EHIR), selected to CB Insights’ Digital Health 150, and named one of Newsweek’s Top Most Loved Workplace® .

With more than $100 million raised in recent funding, including a $53 million Series E round in 2025 led by Maj Invest, and a $50 million investment in 2023 led by Temasek, Twin is scaling rapidly across the U.S. and globally. Backed by leading venture firms like ICONIQ Growth, Sequoia, Sofina, Temasek, and Peak XV, we are building the most impactful digital health company in the world.

Join us as we reinvent the standard of care in metabolic health.

Opportunity

marketing channels: email, direct mail, and digital. This role sits at the intersection of marketing strategy, data, and technical execution. You will turn raw campaign and behavioral data into clear analysis that drives decisions at every level, from channel owners to the executive team.

Right now, the first priority is to understand performance before we optimize it. In your first year you will establish trusted, consistent performance baselines across channels, find where the data does not add up, and tell us what is working and what is not. As that foundation matures, the role grows into attribution, marketing mix, and scoring models that guide budget allocation and targeting.

Our data foundation is built by our data engineering team. You will be its most demanding user. You will query across sources to answer marketing questions, find the gaps and inconsistencies others miss, and tell the data team what needs to be tracked, modeled, or fixed so the next question is easier to answer.

This role is for someone whose edge is judgment. You know what to ask before you write the query, you notice when an answer does not add up, and you give the marketing team a recommendation they can act on. It is a hands-on, high-impact individual contributor role for someone who works independently in a fast-moving environment and is equally comfortable digging through a warehouse and presenting to senior leaders.

Responsibilities

Channel Performance Measurement & Analytics

- Measure and report on performance across email, direct mail, and digital — defining the right metrics, building reporting, and surfacing what is working and what is not
- Own digital analytics end to end, including event tracking and tagging strategy, and partner with engineering to ensure data is captured accurately across web and app properties
- Build and maintain attribution and marketing mix models to quantify channel contribution and guide budget allocation across the marketing portfolio
- Analyze paid channel performance — spend efficiency, ROAS, and incrementality — and translate findings into clear optimization recommendations

Decision support for performance marketing

- Partner with channel owners to turn campaign goals into specific, testable questions, and answer them with analysis before launch, while campaigns are in flight, and after they close
- Analyze channel mix, budget allocation, and pacing using CPM, CPC, CAC, conversion rate, and ROAS, and recommend where to shift spend
- Profile audiences across multiple data sources to size and describe segments for targeting, and recommend who to reach and with what message
- Analyze funnels and landing page performance from impression through registration to enrollment, and recommend conversion rate improvements

Data quality and the data foundation

- Write complex SQL to explore, join, and reconcile data across the warehouse and martech platforms, and validate queries drafted with AI assistance
- Question the data: find gaps, conflicting definitions, and tracking breaks, reconcile numbers across platforms, and raise issues with the specifics the data team needs to fix them
- Define requirements for data engineering, including the events, facts, dimensions, and metric definitions needed to support attribution, mix modeling, and scoring in the future, and explain why each one matters
- Document the metric definitions and logic the marketing team relies on

Data Science & Advanced Modeling

- These responsibilities build on the measurement foundation above. Expect to start by evaluating and directing this work, and to take on more of the build as the data matures.
- Own marketing mix modeling (MMM) end to end — building, validating, and refreshing models that quantify channel contribution, diminishing returns, and saturation to guide budget allocation
- Develop propensity and other scoring models to predict member behavior — conversion, churn, and engagement — and operationalize scores to drive targeting, segmentation, and lifecycle marketing
- Apply Bayesian network analysis and related probabilistic methods to model relationships between marketing drivers and outcomes, quantify uncertainty, and support causal and incrementality analysis
- Partner with data engineering to productionize models, monitor performance over time, and ensure outputs are reliable, explainable, and decision-ready for leadership

Experimentation and testing

- Design, run, and read A/B and multivariate tests, including sample sizing, significance, and interpretation, and recommend what to test next
- Help establish testing standards and maintain a prioritized roadmap of experiments
- Insights and communication
- Present findings and recommendations to marketing leadership and the executive team in a clear, decision-ready way
- Partner with marketing, engineering, data engineering, finance, and product to align on definitions, attribution, and measurement standards
- Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

- 8+ years in marketing analytics, performance marketing analytics, data analytics, or a closely related field
- Sound analytical judgment, shown by examples where you reframed a question, found a flaw in the data, or changed a decision
- Proven experience measuring email, direct mail, and digital marketing performance, including channel mix, budget allocation, CPM, CAC, ROAS, and conversion rate optimization
- Comfort writing and validating complex SQL against a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake preferred), with or without AI assistance. Data engineering is not part of this role.
- Working knowledge of attribution, marketing mix modeling, incrementality, and paid channel analysis
- Experience with scoring and predictive models, such as propensity models, marketing mix models, or Bayesian methods, and with applying them to real marketing decisions. Depth in at least one of these and a working understanding of the others.
- Working knowledge of tracking and instrumentation (UTMs, pixels, tag managers, event taxonomy) and of data modeling concepts such as facts and dimensions, enough to specify requirements and spot problems
- Solid understanding of A/B testing: experiment design, sample sizing, significance, and interpretation
- Experience using AI tools such as Claude in analysis and reporting workflows
- Excellent communication skills, with a track record of presenting analysis to senior leadership
- This remote opportunity is based out of the U.S. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

Preferred

- Agency, e-commerce, startup experience
- Experience with a marketing or product analytics platform (e.g., GA4, Amplitude, Adobe Analytics)
- Familiarity with incrementality measurement and experimentation platforms
- Experience with SQL, Python or R for analysis
- Experience with a BI tool such as Lightdash, Looker, or Tableau, and familiarity with dbt
- Marketing experience in healthcare or another regulated industry
- This remote opportunity based out of the U.S. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

About the Role

The search landscape is evolving rapidly. As AI-driven answers increasingly dominate top search results and user reliance on LLMs expands, search engines and AI platforms prioritize sites that deliver exceptional speed, robust structure, and high domain and topical authority. Consequently, a strong technical foundation plays a critical role in ensuring key web pages are efficiently crawled, accurately interpreted, ranked, and cited. In this environment, a solid technical foundation is essential—it determines whether a website's key pages are effectively crawled, understood, ranked, and referenced.

As a Senior Technical SEO Specialist at Motive, you'll be a core stakeholder in the technical health and structure of our web presence. You'll lead our technical SEO program end to end, from site health & architecture to international SEO and new page launches, as well as incorporate emerging technical AEO/GEO best practices into web structure. You'll also use AI-assisted workflows to find and prioritize the work that will have the most business impact. You'll partner closely with Web Strategy, Web Engineering, Content, Product Marketing, and Growth Marketing. You'll also work alongside teammates focused on content SEO and AI search, so that technical, content, and AI-search work reinforce each other.

What You'll Do

- Lead execution for Motive's technical SEO program, conducting recurring audits covering crawlability, indexation, rendering, redirects, canonical tags, internal link structures, structured data, and page quality.
- Use and help improve AI-assisted workflows that turn crawl and search performance data into a clear, prioritized list of fixes, with human judgment applied before anything ships.
- Make sure priority pages can be accessed, understood, and cited by AI answer engines, covering AI crawler access rules, server-side rendering of key content, structured data, entity signals, and page structure that's easy to extract.
- Identify and resolve content cannibalization and duplication, working with Content and Web to consolidate, redirect, or differentiate pages so each topic has one clear page that ranks.
- Partner with Web Engineering to improve site errors, warnings, and performance issues on key pages & templates, with recommendations tied to impact on traffic and conversion.
- Optimize high-intent product, solution, and industry pages so they rank and convert on non-brand searches.
- Improve information architecture, navigation, and internal linking so our pages connect cleanly and capture long-tail demand.
- Drive technical SEO across our international sites, including hreflang, regional sitemaps, canonical strategy, and localized templates. Partner with regional marketing teams and native-language reviewers so localized pages reflect how local buyers actually search.
- Define technical SEO requirements for new templates, page types, and CMS capabilities, and provide SEO QA for launches, migrations, and redesigns.
- Turn findings into clear, engineering-ready requirements that explain what's wrong, why it matters, and how to fix it.
- Act as the primary technical SEO partner for web and marketing stakeholders, and help non-technical partners understand trade-offs and impact.

What We're Looking For

- 5+ years of technical SEO experience, ideally in B2B SaaS or complex, multi-template environments.
- Bachelor's degree required.
- Deep expertise in crawling, indexation, JavaScript SEO, sitemaps, canonicals, redirects, hreflang, internal linking, Core Web Vitals, performance, and mobile UX.
- Experience scaling information architecture across category, product, long-tail, international, and localized pages.

- Proven partnership with web and engineering teams to deliver technical fixes and measure impact on traffic, leads, and pipeline.

- Strong understanding of AEO, generative search, crawler access, structured data, page architecture, algorithm updates, AI search features, and evolving SEO measurement.

Modern Health

Modern Health is a mental health benefits platform for employers. More about our culture and what you can expect when you join the team:

- “It Takes a Village” culture. Modern Health has a unique and unabashed culture centered around high empathy and high accountability - with a drive to win. - We demonstrate empathy. We have a supportive and diverse culture where we bolster and uplift each other as we pursue our lofty goals. We encourage selflessness and a willingness to support others, fostering a collaborative and respectful environment.
- We exhibit a bias towards action. This is a fast-paced environment. We jump into problems and initiate solutions. We empower our people to make decisions and experiment, iterate, and repeat until we get it right.

Modern Health is a fully remote workforce and a hyper-growth company that is often recognized for its excellence, winning awards such as World’s Most Innovative Companies of 2023 by Fast Company, Top 25 Companies of San Francisco 2023, and 2023 Well-Being Trailblazer Award. To protect our culture and help our team stay connected, we require overlapping hours for everyone. About the role:

The Engagement Marketing Strategist is a strategic marketing partner to our Client Management organization and a key member of the Member Engagement Marketing team. This role will support Client Managers in driving Modern Health awareness, registration, and meaningful member engagement within client populations.

You will bring together audience strategy, lifecycle marketing, behavioral insight, messaging, and channel planning to turn client and member communication needs into clear, effective recommendations and execution plans. You will help move the organization toward a proactive, measurable engagement strategy—while building repeatable approaches that can scale across clients, populations, and global regions.

This is a highly cross-functional individual contributor role for a marketer who can move comfortably between strategic consultation, campaign planning, campaign execution, and performance learning.

What you’ll do:

- Partner closely with Client Managers to understand client goals, workforce needs, business moments, and member engagement opportunities.
- Develop client-specific communication strategies and campaigns to measurably improve awareness, activation, ongoing engagement, and re-engagement in line with client priorities and agreements.
- Equip Client Managers with strategic recommendations, talk tracks, campaign plans, and data-informed points of view to support client-specific goals.
- Advise on audience segmentation, message sequencing, channel mix, localization, timing, calls to action, and measurement.
- Support client launches, open enrollment, benefit changes, new-hire moments, relaunches, and other high-impact opportunities to drive awareness and utilization.
- Develop custom communications and marketing recommendations, balancing client objectives, member needs, operational feasibility, and brand standards.
- Build and improve repeatable playbooks, toolkits, templates, and frameworks that make high-quality engagement strategy easier to deliver at scale.
- Use campaign and population data to identify opportunities, recommend tests, evaluate performance, and improve future campaign strategies.

What success looks like:

- Establish trusted partnerships with Client Managers and become a go-to advisor for client and member communications.
- Create a clear, repeatable approach for developing client-specific engagement strategies.
- Improve the quality, consistency, and strategic value of recommendations presented to clients.
- Demonstrate measurable progress against agreed-upon engagement outcomes and use learnings to inform future recommendations.
- Help the Member Engagement Marketing team operate more proactively and strategically, with less reliance on one-off, reactive support.

What you bring/ Requirements:

- 5–8 years of experience in lifecycle marketing, customer marketing, member engagement, client strategy, integrated marketing, or a related field.
- Experience developing communication or engagement strategies for multiple audiences, customers, clients, or market segments.
- Experience planning and executing multi-touch, multi-channel campaigns and understanding how audience, message, timing, and channel work together.
- Strong strategic consulting skills, with the ability to understand a business need, identify the underlying opportunity, and recommend a focused path forward.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to make complex ideas clear and persuasive for both internal and external audiences.
- Comfort using data and performance insights to make recommendations, prioritize opportunities, and improve campaign effectiveness.
- Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple clients, priorities, and stakeholders in a fast-moving environment.
- Proven ability to influence without authority and build alignment across cross-functional teams.
- A member- or customer-centered mindset and a high bar for clarity, relevance, and inclusive communication.

- Experience in healthcare, behavioral health, benefits, employee engagement, SaaS, or another complex, high-consideration product or service.

- Experience working across global audiences, languages, regions, or culturally diverse populations.

Tines is the intelligent workflow company that powers some of the world's most important workflows.

Tines has been supporting IT and security teams from a diverse range of customers, including Canva, Reddit, SAP, Coinbase, Mars, Fin (Intercom), and McKesson.

Tines 3B, launched in 2026, is the next generation of Tines – a single, secure environment for every team’s apps, agents and automations.

About the role

In this role, you’ll develop a customer-centric narrative for Tines’ platform capabilities. You’ll work closely with product, engineering, commercial, and marketing teams to turn technical capabilities into clear positioning, compelling content, and effective product launches.

IT will be a priority audience, and you’ll help us reach customers and decision-makers across other lines of business. Working alongside our audience product marketers, you’ll connect a consistent platform story to the problems different business teams need to solve.

You’ll be a leading voice on where Tines fits in the evolving AI landscape. This is a hands-on opportunity for someone who enjoys building with the product, forming a defensible point of view, and turning that thinking into work our teams and customers can use.

You can work remotely within the US but must in an eastern or central state.

What you will be doing:

- Market research. Conduct customer interviews and win/loss research, follow AI developments, and contribute to analyst engagement. Turn what you learn into recommendations for our positioning and go-to-market approach.
- Competitive intelligence. Understand emerging competitors and established alternatives. Translate research into differentiation, battlecards, objection-handling resources, and training.
- Positioning and messaging. Create a clear narrative for what customers can build, run, and monitor with Tines. Partner with product marketers to make it relevant to IT and expanded audiences.
- Product launches. Lead product marketing for new platform capabilities, from identifying audiences and use cases through launch messaging, content, enablement, and measurement.
- Enablement. Partner with Sales Enablement and customer-facing teams to build confidence in our positioning and equip them to address questions from customers, business decision-makers, and technical evaluators.
- Content and collateral. Create practical resources, including blogs, decks, webinars, guides, and product collateral. Work with Content Strategy and experts across engineering, solution engineering, customer success, and support to make our story accurate, credible, and useful.

What you bring with you:

- 8+ years of experience across product marketing, marketing, product management, technical or operational roles, or strategy consulting, including at least three years of direct product marketing experience.
- Experience marketing a technical B2B software product in a fast-moving environment, with an understanding of how enterprise teams evaluate and buy software, particularly within IT.
- Strong positioning and messaging skills, with outstanding written and verbal communication. You can simplify complex concepts without losing accuracy and adapt a narrative for different audiences.
- Practical experience using AI to solve business problems, curiosity about the market, and the ability to discuss its strengths and limitations. You enjoy learning a product by building with it.
- Experience launching products or capabilities and bringing them to new audiences, including identifying use cases, understanding personas, and developing go-to-market programs.
- Strong research and analytical judgment. You can turn customer insight and competitive intelligence into a clear point of view, then use feedback and results to refine it.
- Comfort balancing strategic, creative, and tactical work. You take ownership, prioritize effectively, and create content and enablement yourself.
- Proven ability to build strong cross-functional relationships across distributed teams. You can earn support for a recommendation, defend it thoughtfully, and change your approach when the evidence calls for it.

Compensation: $175,000-$185,000 + equity

At Tines, we’re all about trying new things and taking the leap. If you’re second-guessing your application, we hope you’ll trust your gut and take the leap too! Applying for a new job isn’t always easy, especially if you’re thinking of a career pivot – but we’re big believers in learning and growth here at Tines, so you’ve nothing to worry about. A variety of experience, perspectives, and voices makes us the company we are. We’d love to hear from you.

The Paid Advertising Senior Performance Analyst is responsible for owning the execution, performance, and growth of their marketing service within their book of business. - Oversee high-quality campaign execution, including thorough QA to prevent revenue-impacting errors.
- Ensure accurate budget pacing and advise on budget changes.
- Lead proactive strategy recommendations across assigned channels, surfacing opportunities and risks ahead of client requests.
- Maintain client testing roadmaps and project manage next steps, ensuring a consistent, ongoing cadence of experimentation.
- Escalate performance risks early, distinguishing normal fluctuation from genuine account risk requiring intervention.
- Maintain excellent communication with clients and internal teams, leading strategic conversations and performance discussions.
- Mentor and elevate team talent through coaching, training, and support; identify department knowledge gaps and partner with leadership to implement solutions.
- Conduct training sessions on platforms, tools, industry trends, and best practices to strengthen team capability.
- Collaborate on new business pitches and audits, contributing strategic insights and industry perspective.
- Demonstrate full knowledge of the Power Circuit, executing on all recommendations from the solutions roadmap.
- Leverage AI technologies to optimize workflows, insights, and performance; model best practices for team adoption.

Role Requirements:

- 5-6 years of digital marketing experience; 4+ years in an agency setting
- Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience with Search Engine Marketing
  - Specifically having experience with campaign development and optimization processes such as bid optimization, keyword research, and ad copy development on large, enterprise-level accounts
  - Significant campaign management experience in 3 or more of the following additional campaign types:
    - Performance Max
    - Standard Shopping
    - YouTube Ads
    - Display Advertising
    - Local campaigns
    - Bing Ads

- Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience with Meta ads direct response campaigns
  - Additional platforms a plus (TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Pinterest Ads, etc.)

- Lead Gen and B2B experience

- Proficiency in Google/Microsoft Office Suite(s)
- Proficiency in Google Analytics
- Expert knowledge of funnel marketing and paid advertising in the marketing funnel
- Strong ability to formulate meaningful insights from marketing data, going beyond the stats and telling the story
- Other skills required:
  - Strong written and verbal communication skills
  - Strong organizational and project management skills
  - Self-motivated individual with a strong desire to succeed
  - Excellent interpersonal skills
  - Confident with client-facing presentations and communication
  - Strong work ethic and ability to learn quickly and independently
  - Interested in a long-lasting relationship with a growing company

- Client Retention (bi-annual): 90%

- Audits and supports on strategy across 8-10 existing accounts within the department to ensure the gold standard each quarter
- Plays an active role in team-member development within the department

- Experience auditing and consolidating fragmented communication systems into a single platform and coherent architecture
- Strong analytical mindset with experience segmenting audiences, analyzing cohort/journey performance, and executing hypothesis-driven A/B tests.
- Exceptional copywriting skills, with the ability to write clear, engaging, human-sounding content tailored to business owners.

You will own the strategy and the execution of every proactive, non-clinically led communication a Twin member receives: email, SMS, in-app and push campaigns, direct mail testing, member webinars, and additional channel exploration we have not yet tried. You will design how those communications layer into the care team relationship and the product notification ecosystem already in place.

This is a build role requiring both strategic vision as well as executional know how. Twin members, data, clinical outcomes, and Braze infrastructure is already in place. What does not exist is a deliberate lifecycle program. You will write the strategy, then ship it yourself. We are looking for someone who can point to campaigns they personally built and outcomes they personally moved.

Responsibilities

Active Member Strategy and Program Ownership

- Map the member journey to build sustained engagement, as well as winback for lapsed members, and define the communication strategy for each stage, including who we deliberately choose not to message.
- Own the annual and quarterly engagement roadmap, with a defined direction on stage involvement
- Build a segmentation model grounded in real member behavior, sensors, app engagement, care team interaction, clinical trajectory, enrollment channels, etc.
- Govern the member communication calendar across marketing, care team, product, and clinical, so members experience one coherent voice instead of four uncoordinated ones.

Integration with the Care Team and Product Ecosystem

- Inventory the existing touchpoint landscape and maintain that map as the source of truth.
- Partner with Care Delivery and Clinical leadership to define the boundary between a marketing communication and a clinical one. Member marketing should make the care team more effective, not compete with it for attention.
- Design suppression, frequency capping, and quiet-hours logic across all channels so total message volume stays deliberate as the program scales.
- Work with Product on campaign-based push and in-app messaging
- Ensure deployment accuracy by accounting for the operational realities of the point solution ecosystem: eligibility files, employer and health plan communication rules, benefits calendars, co-branding constraints, and the fact that our members are often being messaged by three other vendors the same week.

Execution, Platform, and Analysis

- Build and ship campaigns end to end in Braze: audience logic, Canvas and journey build, content, QA, launch, and iteration.
- Write copy and creative briefs, and manage design, clinical and legal review as needed to deliver timely campaigns on schedule.
- Develop the Braze instance as it matures: event taxonomy, catalog and Connected Content usage, template library, preference center, deliverability and sender reputation, and the data contract with our Snowflake warehouse.
- Stand up a formal testing program: subject lines and creative to start, then channel mix, cadence, timing, incentive structure, and a direct mail pilot
- Measure performance and build dashboard in partnership with Marketing operations to showcase campaign efficacy
- Report results to Growth Marketing and the broader leadership team on a regular cadence, including wins, losses and adjustments as a result.
- Maintain compliance discipline throughout — HIPAA, PHI handling, TCPA and consent management for SMS, CAN-SPAM, and internal clinical review.
- Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Required

- 4–7 years in lifecycle, CRM, retention, or engagement marketing, with meaningful time spent owning programs end to end rather than executing someone else’s brief.
- Hands-on Braze expertise. You can build a multi-branch Canvas with behavioral triggers, Liquid personalization, and proper suppression logic without waiting on engineering.
- Real multi-channel experience including email plus at least one of SMS, push, or in-app
- Demonstrated experimentation rigor: you design tests with holdouts, understand what a result can and cannot support, and are comfortable reporting a null.
- Comfort building and defining processes. This program does not exist yet; you will be building the first version.

Strongly Preferred

- Healthcare or digital health experience, with working fluency in HIPAA and PHI handling in marketing systems.
- Direct experience in the point solution ecosystem: a digital health, condition management, or benefits vendor distributed through employers, health plans, or health systems. You understand eligibility-driven populations, client communication approvals, and the practical difference between enrollment marketing and active member marketing.
- Experience marketing alongside a human care team or clinical staff
- Exposure to offline or physical channels (direct mail, print, or member webinars) and how to measure them.

How We Will Measure Success

- Channel metrics matter, but they are not the scoreboard. In the first year, this role will be evaluated on:
- Member activation:  speed and rate of getting new members fully onboarded and using the program as designed.
- Sustained engagement: sensor wear, app usage, and care team interaction over time, particularly past the point where members typically plateau.
- Retention — reduced member attrition
- Clinical outcomes — increased milestone achievements directly impact the bottom line for Twin. Program maturity — a functioning lifecycle engine: documented strategy, healthy deliverability, a running test backlog, and reporting the business trusts.
